identity.real_world_identity_notes: Maserati specifies an eight-speed dual-clutch transmission, carbon-fibre paddle shifters, and wheel-integrated shift lights; exact AMS2 move-off and shift behavior were guided-tested separately.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed round rim with wheel-mounted shift lights and no integrated display.

notes: The modeled dual-clutch system moved the car from rest without physical clutch input.
All eight paddle-selected gears accepted clutchless shifts and automatic downshift blip was directly observed.
A throttle-channel dip during an upshift was later found insufficient to establish an automatic ignition cut; that field remains unknown.
Guided test completed in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch and Auto Shifting disabled and no separate throttle-blip assist available.
The observed throttle-channel dip could reflect driver input, traction control, or telemetry filtering, so automatic cut remains unknown.

confidence.basis: Manufacturer sources and exact guided testing agree on the eight-speed paddle-operated dual-clutch interface and automatic blip; automatic cut is not established.

claims.basis: Official release context and exact live telemetry establish the simulator identity and class.
Maserati documentation and exact live testing agree on eight-speed dual-clutch paddle operation.
Guided current-game testing directly established move-off, downshift blip, and wheel details.

driver_summary: Road dual-clutch: it blips its own downshifts, cuts its own upshifts and needs no clutch to pull away. The paddles ask the box for a gear rather than telling it, and it can refuse one that would over-rev the engine.
